description: Plan a growing season from field assessment through planting schedule to input requirements.

steps.description: Assess field conditions including soil test results, drainage, and rotation history.

inputs.name: soil-test-results
inputs.desc: Lab results for soil nutrient and pH levels

inputs.name: field-history
inputs.desc: Rotation history and prior crop performance

outputs.name: field-assessment
outputs.desc: Summary of field readiness and constraints

outputs.name: soil-amendment-needs
outputs.desc: Recommended soil amendments before planting

process: Review soil test results for nutrient levels, pH, and organic matter.
Evaluate drainage and compaction from field observation.
Summarize rotation history and any disease or pest carry-over risks.
List soil amendments needed before planting.

steps.description: Select crops based on market demand, climate zone, and field constraints.

inputs.name: market-conditions
inputs.desc: Current commodity prices and demand forecasts

outputs.name: crop-selections
outputs.desc: Selected crops with acreage allocation

outputs.name: expected-yields
outputs.desc: Projected yields per crop per acre

process: Match field conditions to crop suitability by climate zone.
Evaluate market demand and price forecasts for candidate crops.
Allocate acreage across selected crops based on profitability and risk.
Estimate expected yields using historical data and soil quality.

steps.description: Build the planting schedule with dates, varieties, and field assignments.

outputs.name: planting-schedule
outputs.desc: Calendar of planting dates by crop and field

outputs.name: variety-selections
outputs.desc: Specific varieties chosen for each crop

process: Set target planting dates based on frost dates and crop maturity requirements.
Select varieties for each crop based on field conditions and market needs.
Assign fields to crops in the planting rotation.
Build the calendar with sequential planting windows.

steps.description: Calculate seed, fertilizer, and chemical input requirements for the season.

inputs.name: planting-schedule
inputs.desc: Planting dates and acreage by crop

outputs.name: input-list
outputs.desc: Quantities and timing for all inputs

outputs.name: input-cost-estimate
outputs.desc: Estimated cost for all inputs

process: Calculate seed quantities by crop, variety, and seeding rate.
Determine fertilizer application rates from soil test recommendations.
List herbicide and pesticide needs based on field history.
Estimate total input costs and identify bulk purchase opportunities.

steps.description: Set the irrigation plan for the growing season.

inputs.name: crop-selections
inputs.desc: Selected crops and their water needs

inputs.name: field-assessment
inputs.desc: Field drainage and water source data

outputs.name: irrigation-plan
outputs.desc: Irrigation schedule by crop and growth stage

outputs.name: water-budget
outputs.desc: Total water volume and cost estimate

process: Estimate water requirements by crop and growth stage.
Assess the water source capacity and delivery system.
Set the irrigation schedule with frequency and duration.
Calculate the seasonal water budget.

steps.description: Compile the final seasonal crop plan document.

outputs.name: seasonal-crop-plan
outputs.desc: Complete plan for the growing season

outputs.name: milestone-checklist
outputs.desc: Key dates and action items through the season

process: Consolidate the planting schedule, input plan, and irrigation plan.
Create a milestone checklist with critical dates.
Review the plan for conflicts or gaps.
Produce the final seasonal crop plan document.

description: Schedule and manage irrigation based on soil moisture, crop needs, and weather.

steps.description: Collect and interpret soil moisture data across the field.

inputs.name: sensor-readings
inputs.desc: Soil moisture sensor data or manual readings

outputs.name: moisture-profile
outputs.desc: Soil moisture levels by zone and depth

outputs.name: deficit-zones
outputs.desc: Zones below the target moisture threshold

process: Read soil moisture data from sensors or manual sampling.
Map moisture levels to irrigation zones.
Identify zones below the refill threshold.
Flag deficit zones for priority scheduling.

steps.description: Assess crop water requirements by growth stage and evapotranspiration.

inputs.name: crop-stage-data
inputs.desc: Current growth stage for each crop

outputs.name: water-requirements
outputs.desc: Water needs by crop and zone in inches per week

outputs.name: critical-periods
outputs.desc: Growth stages with highest water sensitivity

process: Look up crop coefficient (Kc) for the current growth stage.
Calculate daily evapotranspiration using weather data.
Compute net irrigation requirement minus effective rainfall.
Identify crops in critical water-sensitive growth stages.

steps.description: Evaluate water source capacity and delivery system limits.

inputs.name: system-specs
inputs.desc: Pump capacity, pipe sizes, and emitter rates

outputs.name: delivery-capacity
outputs.desc: Maximum delivery rate by zone

outputs.name: system-constraints
outputs.desc: Bottlenecks or capacity shortfalls

process: Calculate the total water demand across all zones.
Compare demand to pump and well capacity.
Identify delivery bottlenecks (pipe size, pressure, emitter rate).
Flag zones where demand exceeds delivery capacity.

steps.description: Build the irrigation schedule with timing, duration, and method for each zone.

outputs.name: irrigation-schedule
outputs.desc: Run times by zone, day, and duration

outputs.name: water-usage-forecast
outputs.desc: Projected water usage for the scheduling period

process: Prioritize deficit zones for immediate irrigation.
Calculate run times from application rate and requirement.
Sequence zones to stay within pump capacity.
Produce the schedule with start times, durations, and volumes.

steps.description: Adjust the irrigation schedule based on weather forecasts.

outputs.name: adjusted-schedule
outputs.desc: Schedule modified for expected rainfall or heat

outputs.name: adjustment-log
outputs.desc: Record of changes made and reasons

process: Review the precipitation forecast for the scheduling period.
Reduce or skip runs where effective rainfall will meet crop needs.
Increase irrigation before forecasted high-heat periods.
Log all adjustments with the reasoning.

description: Scout, identify, and manage crop pests or diseases from field observation through treatment.

steps.description: Scout the field and document pest or disease symptoms.

inputs.name: field-map
inputs.desc: Map of the field with zones or sections

inputs.name: scouting-observations
inputs.desc: Visual observations of symptoms or damage

outputs.name: symptom-report
outputs.desc: Documented symptoms with location, severity, and photos

outputs.name: affected-area-map
outputs.desc: Map of affected zones and spread pattern

process: Walk the field on a systematic pattern (W or zigzag).
Record symptoms: leaf damage, discoloration, wilting, insect presence.
Photograph representative samples at each location.
Map the affected area and note the spread direction.

steps.description: Identify the pest or pathogen from symptoms and field evidence.

inputs.name: crop-type
inputs.desc: The crop species and variety affected

outputs.name: identification-result
outputs.desc: Identified pest or pathogen with confidence level

outputs.name: biology-summary
outputs.desc: Life cycle, host range, and conditions favoring the organism

process: Compare symptoms against known pest and disease references for the crop.
Check for diagnostic signs (frass, spores, egg masses, feeding patterns).
Submit samples for lab confirmation if field ID is uncertain.
Document the identification with supporting evidence.

steps.description: Assess the severity and rate of spread.

outputs.name: severity-rating
outputs.desc: Severity score and economic threshold assessment

outputs.name: spread-forecast
outputs.desc: Predicted spread based on conditions and biology

process: Rate severity using a standardized scale for the pest or disease.
Compare the infestation level to the economic action threshold.
Forecast spread based on weather, biology, and field layout.
Determine whether treatment is economically justified.

steps.description: Select the management strategy: cultural, biological, or chemical.

outputs.name: management-plan
outputs.desc: Selected control methods with timing and application details

outputs.name: product-list
outputs.desc: Specific products, rates, and pre-harvest intervals

process: Evaluate cultural controls (crop rotation, resistant varieties, sanitation).
Assess biological options (beneficial insects, microbial agents).
Select chemical controls if threshold is exceeded, choosing lowest-impact options.
Set application timing, rates, and re-entry intervals.

steps.description: Apply treatment, monitor effectiveness, and produce the pest management record.

outputs.name: treatment-record
outputs.desc: What was applied, when, where, and by whom

outputs.name: effectiveness-assessment
outputs.desc: Post-treatment evaluation of pest or disease reduction

process: Apply the treatment per the management plan.
Scout treated areas 5 to 7 days after application.
Compare post-treatment pest levels to pre-treatment levels.
Document effectiveness and decide on follow-up action.

description: Plan harvest logistics from maturity assessment through storage management.

steps.description: Assess crop maturity and determine the optimal harvest window.

inputs.name: crop-data
inputs.desc: Crop type, variety, and planting date

inputs.name: field-samples
inputs.desc: Maturity test results (moisture, color, seed fill)

outputs.name: harvest-window
outputs.desc: Optimal start and end dates for harvest

outputs.name: maturity-status
outputs.desc: Current maturity stage by field

process: Test grain moisture or fruit maturity indicators.
Compare to target harvest parameters for the variety.
Factor in weather forecast for the harvest period.
Set the harvest window with start and end dates.

steps.description: Schedule equipment and labor for the harvest period.

outputs.name: equipment-schedule
outputs.desc: Combine, truck, and labor assignments by day

outputs.name: contingency-plan
outputs.desc: Backup plan for equipment breakdown or weather delays

process: Calculate daily harvest capacity based on equipment and field conditions.
Assign equipment and operators to fields in priority order.
Schedule trucking capacity to match harvest throughput.
Plan contingencies for breakdowns and rain delays.

steps.description: Plan transport from field to storage or delivery point.

outputs.name: transport-plan
outputs.desc: Truck routes, schedules, and load assignments

outputs.name: delivery-coordination
outputs.desc: Receiving schedules at storage or elevator

process: Map routes from each field to the storage location.
Calculate truck turnaround times and fleet requirements.
Coordinate receiving schedules to avoid wait times.
Set up communication for real-time dispatching.

steps.description: Set up quality grading and inspection at the receiving point.

outputs.name: grading-protocol
outputs.desc: Sampling plan and quality standards by load

outputs.name: rejection-criteria
outputs.desc: Thresholds for rejecting or downgrading loads

process: Define quality parameters (moisture, damage, foreign material, test weight).
Set the sampling protocol for incoming loads.
Establish acceptance, downgrade, and rejection thresholds.
Train receiving staff on the grading procedure.

steps.description: Manage storage conditions to preserve crop quality.

inputs.name: grading-protocol
inputs.desc: Quality standards for stored grain or produce

outputs.name: storage-management-plan
outputs.desc: Temperature, moisture, and aeration settings by bin or facility

outputs.name: monitoring-schedule
outputs.desc: Inspection frequency and parameters to check

process: Set target temperature and moisture for each commodity.
Configure aeration and drying equipment.
Establish the monitoring schedule (temperature cables, sampling).
Define action thresholds for heating, insect activity, or moisture migration.

description: Build and manage a soil health improvement program from baseline through annual reassessment.

steps.description: Collect baseline soil samples across the operation.

inputs.name: field-map
inputs.desc: Map of fields with management zones

inputs.name: sampling-protocol
inputs.desc: Depth, grid spacing, and lab tests to order

outputs.name: baseline-results
outputs.desc: Lab results for all fields

outputs.name: zone-variability-map
outputs.desc: Map of nutrient and organic matter variability

process: Divide fields into management zones based on soil type and topography.
Collect samples at specified depths following the grid or zone protocol.
Submit samples for analysis (nutrients, pH, organic matter, biology).
Map the results to visualize spatial variability.

steps.description: Set improvement targets based on baseline data and production goals.

inputs.name: production-goals
inputs.desc: Yield and quality targets for the operation

outputs.name: improvement-targets
outputs.desc: Specific numeric targets for key soil health indicators

outputs.name: priority-fields
outputs.desc: Fields ranked by need for intervention

process: Compare baseline values to regional benchmarks and production requirements.
Set targets for organic matter, aggregate stability, water infiltration, and biology.
Rank fields by the gap between current values and targets.
Prioritize fields where improvement has the highest return.

steps.description: Select soil health practices for each field.

inputs.name: improvement-targets
inputs.desc: Target values for soil health indicators

outputs.name: practice-plan
outputs.desc: Practices assigned to each field with implementation timeline

outputs.name: cost-estimate
outputs.desc: Estimated cost per field for the selected practices

process: Evaluate cover crop species and mixes for each field's needs.
Assess tillage reduction options compatible with the cropping system.
Select organic matter additions (compost, manure, crop residue management).
Estimate costs and timeline for each practice per field.

steps.description: Implement the selected soil health practices.

outputs.name: implementation-record
outputs.desc: What was done, when, and where

outputs.name: observation-notes
outputs.desc: Field observations during implementation

process: Execute each practice according to the timeline.
Record application rates, dates, and methods.
Document any deviations from the plan and the reasons.
Note initial field observations after implementation.

steps.description: Resample and compare to baseline to measure progress.

outputs.name: progress-report
outputs.desc: Year-over-year comparison of soil health indicators

outputs.name: updated-plan
outputs.desc: Adjusted practices based on results

process: Resample fields using the same protocol as the baseline.
Compare new results to baseline values for each indicator.
Calculate the rate of change and time to target.
Adjust the practice plan based on what is working and what is not.

description: Manage livestock health from herd protocol through treatment tracking and biosecurity.

steps.description: Establish the herd health protocol covering vaccinations, deworming, and nutrition.

inputs.name: herd-profile
inputs.desc: Species, breed, age groups, and herd size

inputs.name: regional-disease-risks
inputs.desc: Prevalent diseases and parasites in the area

outputs.name: health-protocol
outputs.desc: Vaccination, deworming, and nutrition schedule

outputs.name: product-inventory
outputs.desc: Required vaccines, dewormers, and supplements

process: List required and recommended vaccinations by species and age group.
Set the deworming schedule based on regional parasite pressure.
Define nutritional requirements by production stage (growth, lactation, maintenance).
Create the product inventory and ordering schedule.

steps.description: Schedule and manage routine and emergency veterinary visits.

outputs.name: vet-schedule
outputs.desc: Calendar of scheduled and recommended vet visits

outputs.name: emergency-contacts
outputs.desc: Vet and after-hours emergency contact list

process: Schedule routine herd checks and vaccination visits.
Set up pregnancy checks and reproductive management visits.
Establish the emergency call protocol and contact list.
Budget for veterinary services.

steps.description: Monitor individual animal condition and behavior for early detection.

inputs.name: herd-profile
inputs.desc: Animal IDs and baseline condition scores

outputs.name: condition-scores
outputs.desc: Body condition scores and behavior notes per animal

outputs.name: alert-list
outputs.desc: Animals flagged for follow-up

process: Score body condition on the standard scale for the species.
Observe feeding behavior, mobility, and social interaction.
Compare to baseline and flag animals below threshold.
Record all observations in the herd management system.

steps.description: Track treatments administered and their outcomes.

outputs.name: treatment-log
outputs.desc: Treatments given with dates, products, doses, and withdrawal periods

outputs.name: outcome-summary
outputs.desc: Recovery rates and treatment effectiveness

process: Record the diagnosis and treatment for each animal.
Track withdrawal periods for meat and milk.
Follow up at specified intervals to assess recovery.
Summarize outcomes to identify recurring health issues.

steps.description: Manage biosecurity measures to prevent disease introduction.

outputs.name: biosecurity-plan
outputs.desc: Entry protocols, quarantine procedures, and sanitation standards

outputs.name: compliance-checklist
outputs.desc: Daily and weekly biosecurity tasks

process: Define entry protocols for visitors, vehicles, and new animals.
Set quarantine procedures and duration for incoming livestock.
Establish sanitation standards for facilities and equipment.
Create the compliance checklist for daily operations.

description: Plan farm finances from revenue projection through cash flow management and marketing.

steps.description: Project revenue by crop and market channel.

outputs.name: revenue-forecast
outputs.desc: Projected gross revenue by crop

outputs.name: price-risk-assessment
outputs.desc: Sensitivity of revenue to price changes

process: Calculate gross revenue per crop from yield and price.
Model price scenarios (low, base, high) for each commodity.
Assess revenue risk from yield variability.
Identify the crops with highest revenue certainty.

steps.description: Estimate all input costs for the season.

inputs.name: input-prices
inputs.desc: Current prices for seed, fertilizer, fuel, and labor

outputs.name: cost-breakdown
outputs.desc: Total costs by category and crop

outputs.name: break-even-prices
outputs.desc: Commodity price needed to cover costs per crop

process: List all variable costs by crop (seed, fertilizer, chemicals, custom hire).
Add fixed costs (land rent, equipment payments, insurance, taxes).
Calculate break-even price per bushel or unit for each crop.
Identify opportunities to reduce costs without affecting yield.

steps.description: Plan monthly cash flow for the farm operation.

outputs.name: cash-flow-schedule
outputs.desc: Monthly inflows and outflows

outputs.name: financing-needs
outputs.desc: Months where operating loans are needed

process: Map revenue receipts to the months they arrive.
Map expenses to the months they are due.
Calculate the cumulative cash position by month.
Identify months requiring operating loan draws.

steps.description: Evaluate financing options for operating and capital needs.

outputs.name: financing-options
outputs.desc: Available loan products and terms

outputs.name: financing-recommendation
outputs.desc: Recommended financing structure

process: Identify operating loan options (FSA, commercial bank, Farm Credit).
Compare interest rates, terms, and flexibility.
Assess equipment financing for capital needs.
Recommend the financing structure that minimizes cost.

steps.description: Set the grain or commodity marketing plan.

outputs.name: marketing-plan
outputs.desc: Sales strategy with timing, volumes, and price targets

outputs.name: risk-management-tools
outputs.desc: Hedging or insurance instruments selected

process: Set price targets above break-even for each crop.
Plan the sales calendar (pre-harvest contracts, harvest sales, storage sales).
Evaluate hedging tools (futures, options, basis contracts).
Select crop insurance coverage levels.

description: Set up precision agriculture from field mapping through variable-rate application and profitability analysis.

steps.description: Map the field with GPS boundaries and management zones.

inputs.name: existing-maps
inputs.desc: Any prior maps, aerial photos, or soil surveys

outputs.name: field-boundary-map
outputs.desc: GPS boundaries for each field

outputs.name: management-zones
outputs.desc: Delineated zones based on soil, topography, and yield history

process: Drive or walk field boundaries with GPS to create the boundary file.
Overlay soil survey and topographic data.
Delineate management zones from yield maps, soil type, and elevation.
Export zone maps in a format compatible with field equipment.

steps.description: Collect and clean yield monitor and soil sampling data.

inputs.name: raw-data-files
inputs.desc: Yield monitor files and soil sample results

outputs.name: cleaned-yield-data
outputs.desc: Multi-year yield data with outliers removed

outputs.name: soil-data-layers
outputs.desc: Georeferenced soil nutrient and texture data

process: Import yield monitor data and remove header/end-of-pass errors.
Normalize yield data across years for comparison.
Georeference soil samples to field coordinates.
Combine data layers into a single field database.

steps.description: Create variable-rate application maps from field data.

outputs.name: vra-maps
outputs.desc: Variable-rate prescription maps for seed, fertilizer, and lime

outputs.name: rate-justification
outputs.desc: Agronomic basis for each zone rate

process: Set target application rates for each zone based on soil data and yield goals.
Build the prescription file for the equipment controller.
Validate that rates stay within agronomic and equipment limits.
Document the agronomic justification for each zone rate.

steps.description: Configure equipment for variable-rate input application.

inputs.name: equipment-specs
inputs.desc: Controller type, planter or spreader model

outputs.name: equipment-config
outputs.desc: Controller settings and file transfer instructions

outputs.name: calibration-record
outputs.desc: Calibration checks performed before application

process: Load prescription files onto the equipment controller.
Set the controller to variable-rate mode and verify file compatibility.
Calibrate the applicator (seed drop, fertilizer rate, lime spread).
Run a test pass and verify actual vs prescribed rates.

steps.description: Monitor field conditions in-season using remote sensing or scouting.

outputs.name: vegetation-index-maps
outputs.desc: NDVI or other index maps from drone or satellite imagery

outputs.name: in-season-issues
outputs.desc: Areas of concern identified from imagery or scouting

process: Acquire drone or satellite imagery at key growth stages.
Generate vegetation index maps (NDVI, NDRE).
Compare index values to management zone expectations.
Flag areas for ground-truthing and targeted scouting.

steps.description: Analyze field-level and zone-level profitability.

outputs.name: profitability-map
outputs.desc: Net return per acre by zone

outputs.name: optimization-recommendations
outputs.desc: Zones to increase, maintain, or decrease inputs

process: Calculate gross revenue by zone from yield and commodity price.
Allocate input costs by zone from the VRA prescription rates.
Compute net return per acre for each zone.
Recommend input adjustments for unprofitable zones.

description: Implement on-farm food safety from standard identification through audit preparation.

steps.description: Identify the applicable food safety standard for the operation.

inputs.name: operation-profile
inputs.desc: Crop types, markets served, and buyer requirements

inputs.name: regulatory-context
inputs.desc: Federal and state food safety regulations that apply

outputs.name: applicable-standard
outputs.desc: The standard to comply with (GAP, FSMA, organic, buyer-specific)

outputs.name: requirements-summary
outputs.desc: Key requirements of the applicable standard

process: Determine which regulations apply based on crop type and sales volume.
Identify buyer-specific requirements (third-party audits, certifications).
Select the standard that satisfies regulatory and market requirements.
Summarize the key requirements to address.

steps.description: Conduct a gap assessment against the selected standard.

outputs.name: gap-assessment
outputs.desc: List of gaps between current practices and the standard

outputs.name: remediation-priorities
outputs.desc: Gaps ranked by risk and effort to close

process: Walk through each section of the standard against current practices.
Document gaps where current practices fall short.
Assess each gap for food safety risk.
Rank remediation priorities by risk and implementation difficulty.

steps.description: Implement required practices to close the gaps.

inputs.name: remediation-priorities
inputs.desc: Ranked list of items to address

outputs.name: implemented-practices
outputs.desc: New or modified procedures with effective dates

outputs.name: training-log
outputs.desc: Staff training completed on new procedures

process: Implement water testing at required frequency.
Establish worker hygiene training and facilities.
Set up traceability (lot tracking from field to buyer).
Train all staff on new procedures and document the training.

steps.description: Document procedures and maintain required records.

outputs.name: record-system
outputs.desc: Organized record-keeping system with templates

outputs.name: record-review-schedule
outputs.desc: Frequency for reviewing and updating records

process: Create record templates for each required log (water tests, hygiene, pesticide use).
Set up the filing system (digital or paper).
Establish the review schedule for record completeness.
Assign responsibility for each record type.

steps.description: Prepare for the food safety audit.

outputs.name: audit-readiness-report
outputs.desc: Self-assessment score and items needing attention

outputs.name: audit-binder
outputs.desc: Organized documentation package for the auditor

process: Conduct a self-assessment using the audit checklist.
Organize all documentation in the audit binder.
Walk the facility and fields to verify practices match documentation.
Brief staff on audit procedures and their roles during the visit.

description: File and manage a crop insurance claim from loss documentation through appeal.

steps.description: Document the crop loss with cause, date, and extent.

inputs.name: loss-event
inputs.desc: Description of the loss event (drought, hail, flood, disease)

inputs.name: field-records
inputs.desc: Planting records, input records, and yield history

outputs.name: loss-documentation
outputs.desc: Written description with dates, cause, and affected acreage

outputs.name: photographic-evidence
outputs.desc: Dated photos of damage from multiple angles

process: Record the date and cause of loss as soon as possible.
Document the affected acreage and estimated damage percentage.
Photograph damage from multiple locations across the field.
Gather supporting records (planting dates, input applications, weather data).

steps.description: Notify the insurance agent and file the notice of loss.

inputs.name: loss-documentation
inputs.desc: Description and evidence of the loss

inputs.name: policy-details
inputs.desc: Policy number, coverage type, and agent contact

outputs.name: notice-confirmation
outputs.desc: Confirmation that the notice was filed with date and reference number

outputs.name: adjuster-assignment
outputs.desc: Assigned adjuster name and expected inspection timeline

process: Contact the insurance agent within the required notification period.
Provide the loss documentation and policy details.
Confirm receipt and get the notice reference number.
Note the assigned adjuster and expected inspection date.

steps.description: Coordinate the adjuster inspection and preserve evidence.

outputs.name: inspection-record
outputs.desc: Notes from the adjuster visit and measurements taken

outputs.name: preserved-evidence
outputs.desc: Evidence maintained per policy requirements

process: Do not destroy evidence or harvest the affected area before inspection.
Prepare all records for the adjuster to review.
Walk the field with the adjuster and answer questions.
Record the adjuster's measurements and observations.

steps.description: Review the loss determination and indemnity calculation.

outputs.name: indemnity-calculation
outputs.desc: Expected payment amount based on the determination

outputs.name: discrepancy-list
outputs.desc: Any disagreements with the adjuster findings

process: Review the adjuster's yield appraisal and damage assessment.
Verify the indemnity calculation against policy terms.
Compare the determination to your own loss estimate.
List any discrepancies for potential discussion or appeal.

steps.description: Appeal the determination if the payment is insufficient.

outputs.name: appeal-filing
outputs.desc: Formal appeal with supporting evidence

outputs.name: claim-record
outputs.desc: Complete record of the claim from notice through resolution

process: Decide whether to accept the determination or appeal.
If appealing, prepare additional evidence supporting a higher loss.
File the appeal within the required deadline.
Maintain the complete claim record regardless of outcome.
